terms.gloss: Will you eat here or take it away?
terms.comment: A question of ours: we have found no set phrase for it in the authors searched or in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. It is edere, to eat, and auferre, to carry off, both in the future; the future edēs also keeps clear of ēs, “you eat”, which sounds like es, “you are”. For the food itself, see “fast food”.

phrases.english: To take away, please: we’ll eat at home.
We’ll eat in; there are two of us.

sources: Lewis & Short: edo · Lewis & Short: aufero
